newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vedior targets 10 pct profit growth after float.
newsitem.headline: Vedior targets 10 pct profit growth after float.

text.p: Employment services group Vedior, which floats on the Amsterdam stock exchange on June 5, aims for net profit growth of over 10 percent a year over the next three to four years, Chairman Gert Smit said on Thursday.
Vedior also aims to achieve an annual autonomous growth in turnover of some 10 percent over the same period, but this is likely to be boosted by acquisitions, he said.
"We'll have some one billion guilders ($524.3 million) in cash flow available for acquisitions over the next four years," Smit said.
Vedior is an offshoot of retail and business services group Vendex International which decided to demerge its services arm in January after buying French temporary employment agency BIS.
Vedior aims to achieve a 20 percent market share in the countries where it is currently most active -- France, the Netherlands and Belgium.
"I think we have enough critical mass to achieve a market share of 20 percent in Europe's most important countries," Smit said.
He said the European temporary employment market had a turnover of some 60 billion guilders in 1996 and would grow by ten percent a year until the year 2000 at least.
Some 91 percent of turnover in the sector was generated in just five countries, with France accounting for 31 percent, England for 25 percent and the Netherlands for 16 percent.
"So, we'll notably look for fill-in acquisitions in these countries," Smit said.
A bigger market share would also enable Vedior to further improve its margins.
"I think we have a very big upside potential. Operating profit as a percentage of sales is now at 3.5 percent, and it should go towards four or 4.5 percent," he said.
Growth would be generated by the increasing demand for temporary staff, deregulation and product innovation, Smit said, adding economies of scale were also very important to Vedior.
In the Netherlands, Vedior has a market share of almost 10 percent, well behind the estimated 35 percent of market leader Randstad.
"We can significantly reduce this gap only by making acquisitions," Smit said.
In France, Vedior aims at strengthening its position in the Paris region and is in talks with several companies, he said.
Smit said the French market for temporary employment grew ten percent in the first quarter of this year, accelerating to 15 percent in April.
Vedior is also eager to strengthen its position in Germany and to get a solid foothold in Britain, he said.
"Our preference goes to the Laborman model - we take a minority stake of some 30 percent with an option to fully acquire the company."
Smit said the European cleaning market totaled some 55 billion guilders of sales in 1995 and was mature, with growth rates of under two percent annually.
He said economies of scale would help Vedior to attract big customers, while value-added services would also reduce margin pressure.
"In temporary employment, we're number three in Europe; in cleaning, we're number two," Smit said.

With almost 80 percent of sales generated in temporary employment services and 20 percent in cleaning, Vedior derives 62 percent of its sales from France, 23 percent from the Netherlands and 12 from Belgium and Luxemburg.
Vedior had pro-forma sales in the fiscal year 1996/97 of 6.5 billion guilders, with operating income of 221 million guilders.
Smit said he expected tax pressure to fall to some 32 percent this fiscal year, down from 35 percent last year.
Vedior shares will be priced at floatation between 33 and 37 guilders, which indicates a bourse value of the group of between 3.1 and 3.5 billion guilders.
